To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the involvement and emotional reaction of sales forecasters to a particular product can influence their judgmental adjustments, and 2) these effects may be moderated by the amount of time series information available to the forecasters.

the accuracy of a judgmental forecast depends on the forecaster's level of involvement and emotional reactions to the product, and that the best judgmental forecasts are made by people who do not know anything about the product.
the accuracy of a sales forecast is influenced by the involvement of the forecaster with the product category, and by the forecaster’s emotional response to particular products.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the forecaster's personal involvement and emotional reactions in judgmental adjustments of statistical forecasts.
the role of the forecaster's emotions and involvement in the forecasting process.
the influence of product involvement, emotional reactions, and the forecaster's knowledge on judgmental forecasting.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the more involved the forecaster is with the products and the more positive the emotional reaction, the more the forecast is adjusted and the less accurate the forecast.

, in the case of short time series, it is important that the forecaster has a good understanding of the product category and that the forecaster should not make judgmental adjustments based on their own preferences.
, in the short run, a high level of product involvement is a positive influence on the accuracy of judgmental forecasts.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the more involved the forecaster is with a product category and the more emotional they are towards particular products, the more likely they are to make inaccurate forecasts, but this effect is reduced if they also have knowledge of the time series.
the most accurate forecasts are made when a forecaster has no involvement with the products, but if they do have an involvement, they should not let this influence their judgments.
the most accurate forecasts are produced by those that do not have any involvement with the product, but when this is not possible the best forecasters are those that are most involved.
The main takeaway from our work is that
sales forecasting is a complex process, which is affected by the forecaster's emotional reactions to the product.
the involvement of the sales forecaster in the product category is a crucial factor to consider when designing a sales forecasting process.
the accuracy of judgmental forecasts may be improved by training the forecaster on how to avoid false consensus effects.
